title: Life beyond the summit
paragraphs: Descriptions of elite rank should not be mistaken for a complete social history of Silla. Farmers, craftspeople, traders, religious specialists, and other communities lived under arrangements that may not be visible in narratives centered on royal courts. The ability to hold high office was only one aspect of a broader distribution of security, work, and privilege.

Archaeological remains can reveal differences in burial practice, residence, and material wealth, though translating these differences into exact rank categories is hazardous. An expensive object might express status without identifying a person’s formal administrative position. Keeping these distinctions clear allows the story of hierarchy to remain human rather than schematic.
